title: Morgan's smoke hood used in a tunnel rescue
summary: Inventor Garrett Morgan used his protective smoke hood to rescue workers after a 1916 tunnel explosion under Lake Erie; he later patented a three-way traffic signal.
why: A breathing hood that let rescuers enter smoke- and gas-filled spaces.

notes.problem: 'Pointed the way to gas masks' is unsupported by the source (a common popular claim).

unsung.contribution: Invented a protective smoke hood and used it to lead a rescue in the 1916 Cleveland tunnel disaster.
unsung.recognition: Cleveland papers and officials initially ignored his role; he sometimes hired a white actor to front his invention.
